Alright, the user wants three things: make the logo larger, use a super fancy font that isn’t Claude (i.e., not the Anthropic fonts we currently have), and stop using orange. I’ve already removed the embedded Anthropic font-face blocks and added a Google Fonts link that pulls in Playfair Display (a fancy serif) and IBM Plex Mono (a good open‑source mono). Now I need to actually replace the CSS references that still point to the old Anthropic fonts, change the orange accent colors to something else (the user said “don’t use orange”; earlier I suggested a lavender shade #b89be0 as a nice alternative that matches the teal palette), and adjust the logo size variable to be larger.

First, I should verify where the font families are referenced. The earlier grep showed many lines like `font-family: 'Anthropic Serif';` and `'Anthropic Mono', monospace`. Those need to be swapped to the new Google Font families: `Playfair Display` for the serif and `IBM Plex Mono` for the mono. A simple `sed` substitution will do the trick across the file.

Next, the orange color is defined in several CSS custom properties: `--accent: #d97757;` and also used in a selection background `#d9775733` and `--stroke-color:#d97757;`. I need to replace all occurrences of `#d97757` (the orange) with a new color that isn’t orange. Lavender (#b89be0) was previously mentioned as a good substitute, and it fits the aesthetic. I’ll replace the accent variable, the selection background (preserving the alpha `33`), and the stroke color.

Finally, the logo size is controlled by the CSS variable `--logo-size:min(30vmin,320px);`. To make it larger, I’ll increase the min and max values proportionally. Going from 30vmin/320px to something like 42vmin/460px should give a noticeable but still bounded increase. I’ll substitute that line accordingly.

I need to do all these edits in one go to avoid race conditions with the file being modified between calls. A single `sed -i` command with multiple `s///` expressions separated by semicolons will apply all changes atomically. After the edits, it’s helpful to confirm that no leftover references to the old orange hex or Anthropic fonts remain, so I’ll grep for `d97757` and `Anthropic` (excluding any base64 blocks) and output the matches.

Thus, the appropriate Bash command is:
`sed -i "s/'Anthropic Serif', serif/'Playfair Display', serif/g; s/'Anthropic Mono', monospace/'IBM Plex Mono', monospace/g" slm_alliance.html && sed -i 's/--accent: #d97757;/--accent: #b89be0;/; s/#d9775733/#b89be033/; s/--stroke-color:#d97757;/--stroke-color:#b89be0;/' slm_alliance.html && grep -n 'd97757\\|Anthropic' slm_alliance.html | grep -v base64`

This will swap the fonts, replace the orange accent with lavender, enlarge the logo, and then show any remaining old references for verification. I’ll issue this as a Bash tool call.

arguments.command: sed -i "s/'Anthropic Serif', serif/'Playfair Display', serif/g; s/'Anthropic Mono', monospace/'IBM Plex Mono', monospace/g" slm_alliance.html && sed -i 's/--accent: #d97757;/--accent: #b89be0;/; s/#d9775733/#b89be033/; s/--stroke-color:#d97757;/--stroke-color:#b89be0;/; s/--logo-size:min(30vmin,320px);/--logo-size:min(42vmin,460px);/' slm_alliance.html && grep -n 'd97757\|Anthropic' slm_alliance.html | grep -v base64
